newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks seen tumbling on Deng's death.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks seen tumbling on Deng's death.

text.p: Taiwan share prices are expected to tumble on Thursday following the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, brokers said.
"The market will fall between 100-150 points," said David Yu, vice president for International Investment Trust Co.
Yu said Deng's death likely would impact the market for one week, but may not be enough to change its long-term bullish trend.
"While the political uncertainty cast by the death cannot be ignored, Taiwan's market has enough momentum to weather this storm," he said.
The market, buoyed by widespread expectation of an economic recovery in Taiwan, has finished higher in 11 of the past 13 sessions and gained more than 500 points over that span.
Lee Chung-ying, chairman of Securities and Exchange Commission, said trading would return to normal in one week because political chaos likely would not emerge in China.
"Right now it appears that (China's president) Jiang Zemin has everything under control. In the short future Taiwan's market should resume to reflect fundamentals," Lee told Reuters.
Finance minister Paul Chiu said he did not expect the market to fall too far.
"The news of Deng's deteriorating health has been circulated for a long time, the day (of his death) is expected," Chiu told the state-fund Central News Agency.
"I believe the stock market will not plunge," Chiu said.
On Wednesday the index closed 14.82 points or 0.19 percent higher at 7,656.85 on a frantic turnover of T$156.99 billion.
A 7,500-7,640 range was seen for Thursday.
